name: MessageBranch
summary: Navigation between regenerated assistant responses. Previous / page count / next controls below a Message bubble. Mirrors Vercel AI Elements `MessageBranch` family verbatim (Previous, Next, Page, Selector).

className.description: Pass-through Tailwind / CSS-class hook. The Lumen tokens are bound via <LumenAIProvider>; className is reserved for one-off layout overrides.

children.description: Vercel AI Elements `MessageBranch` accepts a ReactNode subtree. See ./message-branch.md for the full sub-component composition.

keyboard: Tab — focus moves into interactive children in source order; no keyboard trap.
Escape — collapses expandable surfaces (Reasoning, Tool, Confirmation) when applicable.
wcag: 1.3.1 Info and Relationships — semantic ARIA roles assigned per Vercel AI Elements convention.
1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) — text inherits Lumen body tokens which clear 4.5:1 against surface.raised + tint-accent.
2.1.1 Keyboard — every interactive sub-element is keyboard-reachable; no pointer-only affordances.
2.3.3 Animation from Interactions — animated states (streaming shimmer, collapse) honor prefers-reduced-motion.
rules: Token theming flows through <LumenAIProvider> context — never via per-component prop overrides.
The Vercel implementation handles ARIA semantics; Lumen tokens drive the visual layer only.
honor prefers-reduced-motion and prefers-reduced-transparency at the LumenAIProvider boundary.

do: ALWAYS install the implementation via `npx ai-elements@latest add message-branch` before rendering.
ALWAYS wrap the consuming app in <LumenAIProvider> so tokens flow through context.
ALWAYS consult ./message-branch.skill.md for the NEVER rules before composing this primitive into a surface.
dont: NEVER hardcode model names, accent hues, or token values inside this component — all of those live in <LumenAIProvider>.
NEVER fork the Vercel AI Elements implementation — Lumen ships the theme contract, Vercel ships the React TSX; the install-and-theme seam is the entire point.
NEVER apply backdrop-filter on dense conversation surfaces — see AGENTS.md hard rule 16.
